question: Which editing and selection authority may an external text view own while sharing canonical document text, history and other views?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-unbound at queue position 12. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One canonical document owns text changes, history, schema and authored intent; the adapter owns its DOM, local text representation, parser and native commands.
Canonical updates are delivered synchronously and monotonically; an older callback cannot overwrite newer delivered state (docs/vision/plite.md external-text law).
Lifecycle callbacks cannot edit the mounted view or canonical editor; bounded failure recovery reads the latest canonical state without a replay queue.
Exactly one Text, directed UTF-16 selection and patches, version validation and composition ordering are preserved.
External text does not make Plite a code editor; parser configuration stays in the adapter.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-15 audit's 11-unit dispositions, its reproduction and the executed plan's falsified candidates as historical evidence. Rechecked on the live tree createCodeMirrorAdapter.ts (dispatchTransactions publication, the filter: false sites, the absence of the old queue flags and the composition-end microtask) and the monotonic delivery in external-text-runtime.ts. git log shows later commits on these owners (2026-09-18 runtime rebuild, 2026-09-19, 2026-09-27) without a reintroduced queue. The 2026-09-29 IME caret plan only adjusted adapter synchronization before native composition protection.
summary: The job is to edit one canonical Text through a foreign input engine (CodeMirror, textarea) while Plite keeps canonical changes, history, schema and authored intent and each mounted view keeps permissions and retirement. The 2026-09-15 review found deferred canonical feedback replayed out of order (displayed agoodd against canonical Ragood). Live source has the executed fix. createCodeMirrorAdapter publishes one composed action after target.update inside dispatchTransactions, the dispatchingToPlite, pendingReset and scheduleReset queues are gone, canonical transactions bypass local filters, and the only remaining microtask serves composition-end ordering. ExternalTextRuntime tracks a per-entry callback failure revision and refreshes once instead of letting an older delivery overwrite newer state. The strongest breaking alternative, returning the canonical reply from actions.dispatch, adds a second delivery channel to every adapter without a caller need, now that the dispatch boundary orders observers. Deleting the protocol for native-only code rendering, or moving the adapter into Plite, loses jobs the doctrine names.

reconciliation.question: Which editing and selection authority may an external text view own while sharing canonical document text, history and other views?
reconciliation.reason: The recovered execution is the adoption evidence; live source still matches its dispatch-boundary and monotonic-delivery target.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted slot, protocol and ordered dispatch-boundary publication wins. The reproduced defect is fixed without new public API.

Changing the API so actions.dispatch returns the canonical reply instead of calling view.update loses. It adds a second delivery path to every adapter with no independent caller need, and the dispatch boundary already orders observers.
Adding a session, acknowledgement store or transaction manager loses. It duplicates existing actions, mounted lifetime and the commit fence.
Deleting the external-text base layer and rendering code blocks natively only loses the CodeMirror input-engine job that doctrine names and the mixed-view demo uses.
Moving the adapter or protocol into Plate glue or into Plite core loses. DOM coverage, input arbitration and retirement are Plite jobs, while CodeMirror is an optional Plate peer.
proofLimits: Source review only; adapter, contract and browser suites were not rerun here. The plan's package, browser-matrix and paired Chromium scale receipts are historical. Physical IME, assistive technology and keyboard-to-paint latency remain unproven. docs/vision/plite.md carries an unrelated staged hunk that shifts line numbers by seven.
